dati_metodo: Hand-collected 148 financing offers (accepted and declined) made to 51 early-stage high-tech start-ups from the MIT E-Lab program (program began 1995, applicants up to summer 2000), first professional round; regressions of offer acceptance and offered valuation on VC reputation proxies, holding the start-up fixed.

righe.estrazione: Among competing offers made to the same start-up at its first professional round, offers from high-reputation VCs come with lower valuations: the VCs acquire start-up equity at a 10-14% discount. The author concludes that entrepreneurs are willing to accept a valuation discount to access the capital of better-reputed VCs. The evidence is a within-start-up comparison of offers, in a small sample of high-tech start-ups.
righe.citazione: entrepreneurs are willing to accept a discount on the valuation of their start-up in order to access the capital of VCs with better reputations
righe.frase_paper: Hsu (2004) finds that entrepreneurs accept lower valuations from more reputable VCs: high-reputation VCs acquire start-up equity at a 10-14% discount, in a sample of 148 offers to 51 early-stage high-tech start-ups.
righe.frase_slide: Entrepreneurs accept a 10-14% valuation discount to get a more reputable VC (Hsu, 2004)
righe.numero_chiave: 10-14% discount in start-up equity price paid by high-reputation VCs (148 offers, 51 start-ups)
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Small hand-collected sample of 51 MIT E-Lab high-tech start-ups, offers around 1995-2000, first professional round only; our data are all US PitchBook startups with a first VC round in 2012-2019. It concerns VC reputation, not the timing of rounds.
righe.note: Wording is close to the txt's own conclusion. Hsu's evidence is offers to the same start-up, so the term 'accept' reflects entrepreneurs' choices among offers; association-level finding, not a general market-wide estimate.
